2.5 SQL — Create Schema
Run from EC2 SSH session:
mysql -h convoy-tracker-db.cudtjxrtdbql.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com -u convoy_admin -p convoy_tracker
CREATE TABLE users (
  user_id CHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (UUID()),
  google_id VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  first_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  last_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  cell VARCHAR(20), zip_code VARCHAR(10),
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
  expires_at DATETIME, created_at DATETIME DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE TABLE rides (
  ride_id CHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
  organizer_id CHAR(36) NOT NULL,
  ride_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  channel_name VARCHAR(11) NOT NULL,
  channel_psk VARCHAR(512) NOT NULL,
  ride_date DATE NOT NULL, description TEXT,
  zip_code VARCHAR(10), is_public BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
  map_bounds_north DECIMAL(10,7), map_bounds_south DECIMAL(10,7),
  map_bounds_east DECIMAL(10,7), map_bounds_west DECIMAL(10,7),
  map_tile_source VARCHAR(10) DEFAULT "SAT", map_zoom_max INT DEFAULT 18,
  created_at DATETIME DEFAULT NOW(), expires_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (organizer_id) REFERENCES users(user_id)
);
CREATE TABLE invites (
  invite_id CHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (UUID()),
  ride_id CHAR(36) NOT NULL, token VARCHAR(64) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  created_by CHAR(36) NOT NULL, claimed_by CHAR(36),
  claimed_at DATETIME, expires_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  created_at DATETIME DEFAULT NOW(),
  FOREIGN KEY (ride_id) REFERENCES rides(ride_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (created_by) REFERENCES users(user_id)
);
CREATE TABLE enrollments (
  enrollment_id CHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (UUID()),
  ride_id CHAR(36) NOT NULL, user_id CHAR(36) NOT NULL,
  callsign VARCHAR(50), vehicle_type VARCHAR(100),
  enrolled_at DATETIME DEFAULT NOW(),
  status ENUM("active","cancelled") DEFAULT "active",
  FOREIGN KEY (ride_id) REFERENCES rides(ride_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(user_id)
);
3. Authentication — Google Sign-In Strategy
3.1 Online vs Offline States
KEY PRINCIPLE: Never block radio operation on authentication state. If Google Sign-In fails or is unavailable, the mesh map, HUD, GPS tracking, and radio config all continue working using locally cached data.
IMPORTANT: The organizer developer settings gate (long press header) remains independent of Google Sign-In. Uses existing hardcoded password. Do not entangle these two auth systems.
3.2 Google Sign-In Flow
3.3 Off-Network Behavior
4. Radio Write Process — V3.0 Impact Assessment
The radio write engine is the most complex and proven component in GroupTrack. V3.0 must not change it. The only change is where the ride JSON originates.
4.1 Current Radio Write Flow — Proven in V2.4
V3.0 CHANGE: Stage 1 only. The ride JSON source changes from local file to downloaded JSON from RDS. WorkingConfig build, binary build, and all radio write steps are UNCHANGED.
4.2 Ride JSON Source Change
The local JSON cache is the bridge. Downloaded rides save to convoy_events/ exactly like .convoy imports. The radio write engine never knows the difference between a local and downloaded ride.
5. Invite Link Flow — End to End
5.1 Organizer Creates and Sends Invite
5.2 Rider Downloads and Uses Ride
6. Map Area — Ride Creation Dependency
The ride record in RDS stores the map bounding box set by the organizer during ride creation. When any rider downloads the ride via invite, the app automatically starts downloading tiles for that area. No manual selection required.
7. Future Entity Stubs
These do not exist yet but must be architected so they can be added in V3.x and V4.0 without rewriting V3.0 code.
V3.0 API design principle: every GET /ride/{token} response includes an empty extensions object. Future versions populate extensions with waypoints, org info, etc. V3.0 Android clients ignore unknown fields — forward compatible by design.
8. V3.0 Monday Build Order
PREREQUISITE: Resolve offline maps bug first — see GroupTrack_OfflineMaps_Debug.docx. The offline map pipeline must be proven working before automated map download is built.

=== GroupTrack_V3_Implementation_Plan.docx ===
GroupTrack
V3.0 Implementation Plan — Separated Build Strategy
March 29, 2026  |  Branch: feature/convoy-event-ride  |  Gate: Wednesday Field Test
1. Executive Summary
GroupTrack V3.0 migrates from a fully offline standalone app to a cloud-assisted platform. The migration must be built in two completely isolated phases with a hard gate between them — V2.4 Wednesday field test confirmation — to ensure the proven offline radio engine is never destabilized by backend integration work.
The core principle: build everything that has no device dependency first. Schema, service layer, sign-in screen, and API wiring are all safe to build now. The single connection point — replacing the existing ride creation flow with an API-backed version — is the last thing wired, and only after Wednesday confirms V2.4 is solid.
2. Architecture — What Changes and What Doesn't
2.1 Unchanged in V3.0
2.2 What V3.0 Adds
2.3 The Single Connection Point
There is exactly one place where V3.0 wires into existing V2.4 code: the ride creation flow. In V2.4, Create a Ride saves a local JSON file. In V3.0, it POSTs to /rides and saves the response to local cache. Everything downstream — WorkingConfig, radio write, RIDE tab display — is identical because both versions produce the same local JSON.
⚠  This connection point is ONLY wired after Wednesday test confirms V2.4 is stable. All other V3.0 work is built in isolation before that gate.
3. Phase 1 — Isolated Build (Safe Now, No Device Risk)
Everything in Phase 1 can be built immediately. None of these tasks touch existing V2.4 screens, ViewModel state, or the radio engine. If Phase 1 code has a bug, it has zero impact on the working V2.4 build.
3.1 Backend — RDS Schema
Task B-01 — Create RDS Schema
Task B-02 — Verify PHP API Endpoints
3.2 Android — New Files Only (Zero Touch to Existing Code)
Task A-01 — Add API_BASE_URL to ConvoyConfig.kt
Task A-02 — Create ConvoyApiClient.kt (New File)
Task A-03 — Create ConvoySignInScreen.kt (New File)
Task A-04 — Add Invite Deep Link Handler
Task A-05 — Lead Lock UI Buttons
4. Wednesday Gate — V2.4 Field Test
This is a hard gate. Phase 2 wiring does not begin until all Wednesday tests pass. The gate exists to protect the proven offline radio engine from being destabilized by backend integration.
⚠  If FT-04 or FT-05 fail, offline maps must be resolved before Phase 2 begins. Do not start RDS wiring on a build with broken offline maps.
5. Phase 2 — Integration Wiring (Post-Wednesday Only)
Phase 2 wires the isolated Phase 1 components into the existing V2.4 app. Each task has a clearly defined connection point — the exact line of code or screen where the new component touches existing code for the first time.
5.1 Wire Sign-In into App Launch
5.2 Wire Ride Creation to POST /rides
5.3 Wire Invite Generation and Share Sheet
5.4 Wire Automated Map Download on Invite Accept
6. Full Task Sequence — Ordered Build Plan
7. Separation Rules — What Must Never Be Crossed
These rules enforce the isolation between Phase 1 and Phase 2. They protect V2.4 stability during the build period before Wednesday.
8. Environment Reference

1. Executive Summary
GroupTrack V3.0 introduces comprehensive map management enhancements that transform the platform from basic convoy coordination to advanced off-grid navigation and planning. These enhancements integrate V2.5 Map Manager capabilities with V3.0's cloud-enabled services, creating a sophisticated mapping platform for outdoor recreation.

These map enhancements position GroupTrack as a comprehensive off-grid navigation platform, distinguishing it from basic coordination tools. The integration creates network effects through route sharing while maintaining core offline capabilities for field operations.
Architecture Decision: Two independent map systems enable simultaneous planning and convoy operations without conflict. Users can plan routes while participating in active convoys.

);

CREATE TABLE waypoints (
    waypoint_id CHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    latitude DECIMAL(10,7) NOT NULL,
    longitude DECIMAL(10,7) NOT NULL,
    type ENUM('trailhead','staging','hazard','poi') DEFAULT 'poi',
    description TEXT,
    created_by CHAR(36),
    created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    deleted_at DATETIME NULL
);

=== GroupTrack_V3_Online_Offline_Manual_v2.docx ===
GroupTrack
V3.0 Online / Offline Manual
Features, Functions, and Intent
v2  |  April 18, 2026  |  CONFIDENTIAL
Revisions from v1
First-time setup is three steps — Sign In, accept combined Terms & Policy, Dashboard — not four
Terms & Policy is a single existing document covering rider terms, organizer terms, and privacy policy
Subscription mechanics simplified: hardcoded subscribed for all signed-in users during initial V3.0
'Coming Soon' is reserved for mapping functions that are moving to V2.5 — all other incomplete features show placeholders describing intent
iPad implementation noted as pending Monday planning decision — V2.5 or V3.0
1. What GroupTrack Is
GroupTrack is an off-grid awareness platform for any group activity in areas without cell service. It is designed for off-road vehicles, hikers, mountain bikers, overlanders, search and rescue teams, and hunting parties — anyone who needs to coordinate with others in places where phones stop working.
The platform combines three capabilities into a single Android app:
Real-time group position awareness over LoRa mesh radio — no cell tower required
Organized ride management — create, invite, enroll, broadcast — all before you lose signal
Offline maps and trail overlays — downloaded in advance, available everywhere
1.1 The Core Idea — Online Before, Offline During
GroupTrack splits its functionality along one essential boundary: what happens online before a ride, and what happens offline during a ride.
Before the ride, while you still have connectivity, the cloud handles coordination work — creating rides, sending invites, downloading maps, applying radio configurations. Everything gets prepared, downloaded, and cached to the device.
During the ride, when you are out of cell range, everything runs locally. The mesh radio handles position updates between riders. The map tiles are already on the device. The ride configuration is already on the radio. No network calls happen while you are actually riding.
Key principle: the radio never needs the cloud. Authentication failures, network outages, or server problems never interrupt an active ride. Once you have prepared online, the ride works offline — always.
1.2 Platform Support
V3.0 ships for Android. iPad support is under active planning for a future release (V2.5 or V3.0 — to be confirmed). Web-based access and a native iOS port are on the roadmap for later releases.
2. Understanding Feature States in V3.0
As you explore V3.0 you will encounter screens in one of three states. Understanding these helps set expectations for what each screen can do right now.
Why the split? V2.5 is delivering a standalone trail product that addresses mapping functionality in depth — including map source stability, Utah OHV overlays, and a new Planning Map architecture. V3.0 focuses on cloud-based ride coordination. Each release has a clear purpose, and users get a stable foundation at each step.
3. Online vs. Offline Services
GroupTrack presents two service categories. Which one you interact with depends on whether you have connectivity and what you are trying to accomplish.
3.1 How the App Decides Which Mode You Are In
Every app launch, GroupTrack checks three things:
Do I have cached sign-in credentials? (Am I a returning user?)
Is there network connectivity right now?
Are my accepted Terms & Policy version current?
Based on the answers, the app routes you to the right starting screen — the Dashboard if everything is current and you are online, the Convoy Map if you are offline, or sign-in if you are new.
4. Getting Started
4.1 First Install
When you install GroupTrack for the first time, the app launches into a sign-in flow. You need to be connected to Wi-Fi or cell data the first time — account creation requires network access. After first-time setup, the app works offline.
First-time setup is three steps:
Sign In with Google — tap the Google sign-in button, choose your account
Accept the Terms & Policy — a single combined document covering rider terms, organizer terms, and privacy policy
Dashboard — you have landed on the main online services screen
Not ready to sign in? The Skip for now link on the sign-in screen takes you directly to the Convoy Map. You can use offline features (tile download, radio config, import GPX/KML) without an account. Sign in any time later from the menu.
4.2 Terms & Policy
GroupTrack uses a single combined Terms & Policy document that covers:
Rider Terms — how riders use the app and participate in rides
Organizer Terms — additional terms that apply when you become an organizer and create rides
Privacy Policy — what information is collected and how it is shared (notably: your name and email are shared with organizers of rides you follow or enroll in)
The document is shown in full during sign-up. If the document is updated, you are prompted to re-accept the new version on your next app launch.
4.3 What Sign-In Unlocks
Signing in enables all online features. After your first successful sign-in, you can use online features any time you have network access. Offline features are always available whether you sign in or not.
4.4 Subscription Status
GroupTrack operates on a freemium model. Most features are free forever. Organizer features and online ride management are part of the $3.00/month subscription tier.
For the initial V3.0 release, all signed-in users receive full subscription access at no cost. A go-live date will be announced when subscription billing activates. Users active during this period will be notified in advance and will retain access to their ride history and downloaded data regardless of subscription status.
5. Online Features
Online features require network connectivity and a signed-in account. They are organized around the Dashboard, which is the landing screen after sign-in.
5.1 Dashboard
Dashboard is the landing screen for all online services. It is a live data screen, not a button launcher. Three sections stack vertically from top to bottom:
Notifications — system announcements, ride updates, broadcast messages from organizers you follow
Enrollments — rides you are enrolled in, upcoming first, then active, then recently completed
Invites — pending invitations awaiting your accept or decline
Each entry is tappable for more detail. Invites have inline ACCEPT and DECLINE buttons. Enrollments have a VIEW DETAILS button that takes you to the full ride record.
The bottom navigation bar on the Dashboard provides access to the other main online sections: Rides, Explore, Tracks, Profile, Field Radio.
5.2 My Rides
The My Rides screen organizes your rides into tabs:
ALL — every ride you have any relationship to
ENROLLED — rides you have enrolled in as a rider
ORGANIZED — rides you have created as an organizer
COMPLETED — rides that have ended
Tap any ride to see its detail screen — trailhead, planned route, enrollment list, organizer contact. Organizers can also send invites and broadcast messages from this screen.
5.3 Create Ride (Organizer)
Any signed-in user can become an organizer and create rides. The organizer upgrade is available from the Profile screen and is covered by the same combined Terms & Policy document — no separate acceptance flow is needed beyond confirming the upgrade.
Creating a ride requires:
Ride name
Date
Trailhead — selected by tapping the map or picking from your waypoint library
Map area — bounding box for tile download, drawn on the map or defined by an existing route
Description (optional)
Public or private visibility
The SAVE RIDE button stays disabled until both trailhead and map area are set. These gates are highlighted in orange so you know what is missing.
When the ride is saved, GroupTrack automatically generates a unique radio channel name (CONVOY-XXXX) and a random channel PSK. These travel with the ride to every rider who enrolls, so everyone ends up with matching radio configuration.
5.4 Send Invite and Broadcast
From a ride's detail screen, organizers have two ways to invite riders.
Send Invite — Targeted
Send Invite generates a single-use invite link. Share it via:
QR code — display on screen, another person scans with their phone
Copy Link — copies the invite URL to the clipboard
Share Sheet — uses the Android system share sheet for text, email, or messaging apps
Invite link format: grouptrack.org/invite/{token}
Broadcast — Followers
Broadcast sends the ride notification to everyone who follows you as an organizer. Broadcasts are one-time per ride — once sent, the ride is broadcast and cannot be rebroadcast to the same follower list.
5.5 Accept Invite
Tapping an invite link (or scanning the QR code) opens the Invite Accept screen. You see the ride name, date, organizer, a download warning, and a summary of what accepting means.
Accepting does four things:
Downloads the ride JSON to local storage
Starts automatic map tile download for the ride's map area
Sets a flag marking the radio ready to accept the ride's channel configuration
Creates an enrollment record tying you to the ride
You are also offered the option to add the ride to your calendar.
5.6 Explore Rides
Explore shows public rides that organizers have chosen to list publicly. Search by zip + radius, map area, or organizer name. Each public ride shows a small map vignette with the staging area marked, the date, the organizer's contact info, and a FOLLOW option.
5.7 Profile
The Profile screen shows your account information and related entries:
Your name, email, and subscription status
Callsign, vehicle type, zip code (editable)
Email opt-in toggle for broadcasts
Become Organizer upgrade
Ride History link
Following link
Sign Out button
5.8 Ride History
Ride History shows every ride you have participated in, most recent first. For each ride you see:
Name, date, organizer
Organizer's email
Full rider list with email addresses
EXPORT GPX button to save the ride's track to Downloads
Entries can be searched by name, date, or riding area.
5.9 Following
Following is your list of organizers whose rides and broadcasts you want to see. For each organizer you can see their name, email, and optionally phone. Unfollow any time.
5.10 Track Library
Track Library is a public repository of ride tracks donated by participants of organized rides. Filter and search by difficulty, riding area, or recommendation percentage. Tap any track for its detail — map preview, difficulty, recommend %, donor name, and a DOWNLOAD TO DEVICE button. Downloading a track also auto-downloads the map tiles for its area.
6. Offline Features
Offline features work anywhere, with or without network connectivity, and regardless of sign-in status. These are the core operational capabilities — what the app does during a ride.
6.1 Convoy Map
The Convoy Map is the main operational screen. It runs as a background process whenever the app is open. The Convoy Map shows three behaviors based on what is happening, called RideStates:
Lead Lock
In CONVOY and ORGANIZED states, the Convoy Map automatically tracks the lead cart. A Lead Lock slider in settings configures the distance threshold (300 to 1500 feet, default 330 feet) at which a rider is considered the leader.
RECORD and STOP
RECORD starts GPS track recording. STOP ends the recording and prompts for a track name. In ORGANIZED state, STOP also offers a survey (difficulty, recommendation, track donation) before saving.
Map Settings
The Map Settings panel offers: Offline/Online tile toggle, Map type selector (Satellite, Hybrid, Topo), Track Lead Only, Show Downloaded Areas, Track format (GPX/KML), Tile Download Region entry, Zoom range (Z14 to Z18), Overlay Selector entry.
6.2 Map Manager — Coming Soon in V2.5
Map Manager is the comprehensive planning map toolset — tile download regions, waypoint creation, route planning, overlay management, Utah OHV trail data. In V3.0, the Map Manager entry point shows a Coming Soon notice because this functionality is being delivered in V2.5 via a dedicated Planning Map architecture.
Why is Map Manager delivered in V2.5 instead of V3.0? V2.5 is a standalone trail product release focused on map foundation work — multiple map sources, Utah OHV GeoJSON overlays, a new Planning Map separate from the operational Convoy Map. This structure avoids touching Convoy Map's hard-won stability while building out planning features in depth.
Map functions arriving in V2.5's Planning Map:
Find Area — viewport, geocoder, name search, waypoint radius search
Tile Download — draw a region, pick zoom levels, download tiles
Import GPX/KML — bring in tracks and routes from files
Overlay Selector — pick routes, tracks, waypoints to display
Waypoint Library — manage trailheads, staging areas, hazards, POIs
Route Planner — draw routes by tapping waypoints
Utah OHV overlay — motorized vehicle trail data (ships in V2.4 and V2.5)
V3.0 integration points for organized rides (Set Trailhead picker, Set Map Area picker) reference the V2.5 Planning Map once available.
6.3 Field Radio
The Field Radio screen is the interface to the connected LoRa mesh radio. Always accessible, online or offline, signed in or not. The screen shows:
BLE connection status
Active channel name and frequency
Spreading factor and transmit power
Current callsign
Main actions:
Apply Ride Config — push the current ride's channel and PSK to the radio
Apply Master Config — push the master GroupTrack radio configuration
Verify Config — read back the radio's settings and compare to expected
Change Long Name to LEAD — set callsign to LEAD for the lead rider
Bluetooth Toggle Reconnect — cycle BLE to recover from disconnects
Applying ride config is what gates participation in an organized ride. If your radio does not have the correct channel and PSK, you are invisible to the organized mesh. Apply ride config before leaving the trailhead.
6.4 Archive and Restore
The Archive and Restore screen manages saved radio configurations. Every time you apply a new configuration, the previous one is automatically archived. You can restore any archive to quickly revert. Archives are listed by date and time with a human-readable summary.
6.5 Import GPX/KML
Import GPX/KML lets you bring tracks and routes from outside sources. Flow:
Tap Import GPX/KML
Android file picker opens
Choose Route or Track
Give it a name
MD5 duplicate check runs
File saved to local library; appears in Overlay Selector
6.6 Your Tracks
Distinct from the online Track Library, your personal recorded tracks live locally on the device. You can view, overlay, export as GPX or KML, share, and delete. Accessible through Map Settings → Export Tracks, which opens the file manager at your tracks folder.
7. Understanding RideStates
RideState determines how the Convoy Map behaves. It is computed automatically based on two inputs: how many riders are on the mesh radio, and whether a formal ride record matches today's date and the current radio channel. You do not set RideState manually.
7.1 Mode 1 — Solo Trail Mapper
SOLO is GroupTrack as a personal GPS mapping app. No radio needed, no other riders, no account required. Download offline tiles, record GPS track in real time, export the track afterward. This is the entry-level experience.
7.2 Mode 2 — Ad Hoc Convoy
CONVOY is an impromptu group ride. Somebody brought the radios, everybody has GroupTrack, you meet up and head out. No organizer, no formal ride record. Full convoy map experience — lead lock, mesh positions, HUD — but no tracked ride. Tracks saved locally.
7.3 Mode 3 — Organized Ride
ORGANIZED is the full platform experience. An organizer created a ride, riders enrolled online, maps downloaded automatically, radio configs applied. At the trailhead, everyone shows up matched. The ride is tracked.
ORGANIZED adds to CONVOY:
Planned route displayed on the map in solid orange
Trailhead marker at the starting point
Full HUD with ride-specific callsigns
Survey prompt on STOP — difficulty, recommendation, track donation option
Track donation — your recorded track can be shared to the public Track Library
8. What Happens Online, What Happens Offline
8.1 Online Operations
Sign-in and registration
Terms & Policy acceptance and re-acceptance
Dashboard load (notifications, enrollments, invites)
Ride creation
Invite generation
Broadcast send
Invite accept (downloads ride + tiles)
Profile edits
Follow / unfollow organizers
Explore Rides search
Track Library browse and download
8.2 Offline Operations
Convoy Map (all three RideStates)
Lead lock calculation
GPS track recording
Offline tile rendering from downloaded tiles
Radio configuration
Import GPX/KML from the file system
Archive and Restore
Track export to Downloads
8.3 Deferred Until Connectivity
Post-ride survey submission — queued, uploaded on next connectivity
Track donations — queued, uploaded on next connectivity
Sign-in retry if registration was pending — automatic on connectivity recovery
9. Core Workflows — End to End
9.1 Organizer — Creating and Running a Ride
Online: sign in, open My Rides, tap Create Ride
Online: fill in ride name, date, description. Set trailhead. Set map area. Choose visibility.
Online: tap SAVE RIDE. Ride posted to cloud. Unique channel and PSK generated.
Online: from ride detail, SEND INVITE. Share QR / link with riders.
Online: optionally BROADCAST to followers.
Offline at trailhead: Field Radio → Apply Ride Config. Verify.
Offline during ride: Convoy Map in ORGANIZED state. RECORD your track.
Offline at end: STOP. Survey dialog. Rate difficulty, optionally donate track. Save.
Back online: survey and donation upload automatically. Ride appears in Ride History.
9.2 Rider — Enrolling and Joining a Ride
Online: receive invite link (text, email, QR)
Online: tap invite. Invite Accept screen shows details.
Online: ACCEPT. Ride downloads, tiles auto-download, radio config prepared. Optional calendar add.
Offline at trailhead: Field Radio → Apply Ride Config. Verify.
Offline during ride: Convoy Map in ORGANIZED state. See every mesh rider. Lead lock active.
Offline at end: STOP. Save track, optionally answer survey.
Back online: participation recorded in Ride History.
9.3 Solo Rider — Mapping Without a Radio
Online or offline: open the app. Sign in or skip.
Online once (V2.5+): open Planning Map, Tile Download. Pre-download your area.
Offline at trail: Convoy Map opens in SOLO state.
Offline: RECORD. GPS trail draws in real time on offline tiles.
Offline: STOP and name your track.
Export track as GPX or KML. Share if desired.
10. Frequently Asked
What happens if I lose signal during a ride?
Nothing changes. The app is already running offline during the ride. Mesh radio positions keep updating, GPS track keeps recording, the map keeps rendering from downloaded tiles. You only notice when you try to open Dashboard or other online-only features — those show an offline banner.
What if I never sign in?
You can use GroupTrack fully as an offline mesh-and-mapping tool without signing in. Convoy Map, tile download, radio config, Import GPX/KML, Archive/Restore, and track recording all work. You cannot participate in organized rides, send invites, or see the Track Library until you sign in.
Can I use GroupTrack without a radio?
Yes. In SOLO mode, the app functions as an offline GPS mapping tool. A radio becomes necessary only when you want to see other riders on the mesh or participate in organized rides.
Why are map planning features marked Coming Soon?
Map planning features are being delivered in V2.5 on a dedicated Planning Map, separate from the operational Convoy Map. This keeps the Convoy Map's stability intact while building out planning features in depth. V3.0 links to these features; V2.5 delivers them.
How do map tiles get downloaded?
Three ways. First, manual download from Map Manager (V2.5 Planning Map) by drawing a box and picking zoom levels. Second, automatically when you accept an invite to an organized ride. Third, automatically when you download a track from Track Library.
Where are my tracks stored?
On your device, in your app's private storage. Accessible through Map Settings → Export Tracks, which opens the file manager at your tracks folder. From there you can move, share, email, or delete individual files.
What happens to my data if I uninstall?
Locally stored data (tracks, imported files, downloaded tiles, waypoints) is removed by Android on uninstall. Cloud data (account, ride history, Track Library donations) remains on the server and is available again when you reinstall and sign in.
Can I use GroupTrack alongside the community Meshtastic app?
Yes, beginning with the package identifier migration. GroupTrack installs under its own unique package identifier, allowing both apps to coexist on the same device with independent data and paired radios.
When will iPad be supported?
iPad support is actively being planned — either as part of V2.5 or V3.0. The exact release target will be confirmed in upcoming planning discussions. iOS native phone support is on the later roadmap.

RideState | When Active | What You See

State | Trigger | Mesh | Ride Record
SOLO | One or no riders on mesh, no ride loaded | None or just you | None
CONVOY | Multiple riders on mesh, no ride loaded | Multiple riders | None
ORGANIZED | Multiple riders on mesh AND matching ride loaded | Multiple riders | Matches channel + date
Term | Meaning
Apply Config | Writing a radio configuration to the connected LoRa device
Archive | A saved snapshot of a previous radio configuration, available for quick restore
Broadcast | One-time notification sent by an organizer to all their followers about a ride
Callsign | Short identifier displayed for each rider on the Convoy Map and HUD
Channel | Meshtastic radio channel name and pre-shared key that defines a mesh group
Convoy Map | Primary operational map — mesh positions, GPS trails, lead lock, HUD
CONVOY (RideState) | Ad-hoc group ride — multiple riders on mesh but no formal ride record
Dashboard | Landing screen for online services — notifications, enrollments, invites
Enrollment | Record tying a rider to a specific organized ride
GPX / KML | Standard file formats for GPS tracks and routes
HUD | Heads-up display on the Convoy Map — heading, speed, distance, lead/tail info
Invite | Shareable link or QR code enrolling the recipient in a specific ride
Lead Lock | Automatic identification and tracking of the front rider
Map Manager | Full-screen planning toolset delivered in V2.5 on the Planning Map
Master Config | Default GroupTrack radio configuration applied to new installations
Mesh | Peer-to-peer LoRa radio network formed by Meshtastic radios in range
ORGANIZED (RideState) | Formal ride mode — mesh active and ride record matches channel + date
Organizer | User who creates and manages rides
Overlay | Visual data layer on top of map tiles — routes, tracks, waypoints, trail data
Planning Map | Dedicated V2.5 map interface for planning functions — separate from Convoy Map
PSK | Pre-shared key encrypting mesh radio traffic on a given channel
RideState | Auto-computed mode — SOLO, CONVOY, ORGANIZED — determining Convoy Map behavior
Route | A planned path, drawn before riding — distinct from Track
SOLO (RideState) | Personal mode — no other riders on mesh, no ride loaded
Survey | Post-ride questionnaire for ORGANIZED rides — difficulty, recommendation, track donation
Terms & Policy | Single combined document covering rider terms, organizer terms, and privacy policy
Tile | Small square image of a map region at a specific zoom; maps are made of many tiles
Track | A recorded GPS path — distinct from Route
Track Donation | Optional upload of your ride track to the public Track Library after an ORGANIZED ride
Trailhead | Starting point of a ride; marker displayed on the map in ORGANIZED state
Waypoint | Saved geographic point of interest — trailhead, staging, hazard, POI

Standard | Rule
Email tappable everywhere | Any email address displayed anywhere in the app launches device email client with address pre-populated. No exceptions.
PHP API patches | NEVER use heredoc from Windows Git Bash or Python tempfile from Windows. Always SSH to server and use python3 -c on server side. Always snapshot before changes.
V3 feature gate | All V3 features gated behind V3_FEATURES_ENABLED = false. V2.4 testers unaffected.
One change at a time | Write → build → test → commit. No stacked unverified changes.
Tile migration | On Play Store release: renameTo() moves tiles from debug to release package. No copy — same partition, zero extra space.

=== GroupTrack_V3_Registration_Paywall_Spec_v2.docx ===
GroupTrack
V3.0 Registration & Stubbed Paywall Specification
v2  |  April 18, 2026  |  Walkaway Gate Document  |  CONFIDENTIAL
Revisions from v1
isSubscribed() is now hardcoded to return true with inline activation instructions — no PAYWALL_ENABLED flag
Rider Terms, Organizer Terms, and Privacy Policy are a single combined document that already exists — collapsed former s02 and s03 into one Terms & Policy screen
Placeholder screens for non-working features describe intent; 'Coming Soon' is reserved for mapping functions that are moving to V2.5
iPad implementation scope (V2.5 vs V3.0) flagged for Monday's planning discussion — not resolved in this document
1. Purpose and Scope
This document specifies the complete V3.0 registration flow and the stubbed paywall design. It is the gate document for V3.0 walkaway: until registration is built, stubbed-function definitions cannot be meaningfully reviewed because most V3 stubs depend on an authenticated user_id.
Registration is the entry point for all V3.0 online functionality. Every downstream screen (Dashboard, My Rides, Create Ride, Invite, Explore, Profile, Track Library) depends on a valid user_id cached locally from the registration flow.
Scope:
Registration flow — s01 Sign In through s04 Dashboard, including the combined Terms & Policy screen
Session persistence — SharedPreferences cache fields, offline behavior, re-acceptance triggers
Paywall as stub — s01b built and navigable; isSubscribed hardcoded true at walkaway
Online/Offline auth boundary
Go-Live activation steps — the minimum set of code changes to flip subscription from stub to live
Build inventory — what exists, what needs completion, per file
2. Stub and Placeholder UX Pattern
V3.0 walkaway produces a fully navigable app. Every screen in the V3 user flow opens and does something sensible. Three states exist for any given screen:
No non-mapping screen in V3.0 shows a 'Coming Soon' banner. Either the screen works, or it clearly describes its intent as a placeholder. This ensures V3.0 is a complete-feeling product at walkaway even though Phase C wiring continues toward go-live.
3. Registration Flow Overview
Registration runs top-to-bottom exactly once per user on the installed device. After successful completion, subsequent app launches use cached credentials and route directly to the Dashboard (s04) or the Convoy Map depending on online state.
3.1 Top-Level Launch Routing
App launch
   |
   v
ConvoySessionManager.resolveLaunchRoute(context)
   |
   |-- No cached user_id          --> s01 Sign In
   |-- Cached, terms current      --> s04 Dashboard
   |-- Cached, terms outdated     --> s02 Terms & Policy (re-accept)
   |-- Cached, offline            --> Convoy Map (never blocks radio)
3.2 First-Time User Path
Four screens, executed in order:

4.1  s01 — Sign In
File: ConvoySignInScreen.kt (EXISTS, partial)
Purpose
First-time authentication entry point. Google One Tap acquires a Google ID token, exchanged for a GroupTrack user_id via POST /users/register.
UI Elements
GroupTrack logo and tagline

Skip for now link — offline-only use (radio-only riders)
Brief copy explaining what sign-in unlocks
Behavior
User taps Sign In with Google
Google One Tap displays account selector
User selects account, grants profile scope
SDK returns ID token, email, first/last name
App calls ConvoyApiClient.registerUser()
On success, user_id cached via ConvoySessionManager.saveUser()
Route directly to s02 Terms & Policy (paywall bypassed by hardcoded isSubscribed=true)
Error Handling
Google Sign-In failure: error banner, offer retry or Skip for now
Network failure during registration: cache Google creds, mark registration_pending=true, route to Convoy Map, retry on connectivity

Display and capture acceptance of the single combined Terms and Policy document covering rider terms, organizer terms, and privacy policy. Version tracking triggers re-acceptance when the document is updated.
Rider Terms, Organizer Terms, and Privacy Policy are a single document that already exists. There is no separate Privacy screen, no separate Organizer Terms screen at signup. s06 Become Organizer references this same document for organizer-specific acceptance at upgrade time.

Decline and Exit link
Behavior

User reviews, checks I ACCEPT, taps CONTINUE
Cache accepted version: SharedPreferences key terms_accepted = version string
POST /users/accept-terms with user_id, version, timestamp
Route to s04 Dashboard
Version Mismatch Re-Acceptance
On every launch, compare cached terms_accepted against the current published version. Mismatch triggers routing to s02 on next sign-in regardless of other state. Cached version updated only on fresh acceptance.

5.2 Hardcoded isSubscribed — Walkaway Implementation
The isSubscribed() function is the single point of control for subscription gating. At walkaway it is hardcoded to return true. Activation instructions are embedded as comments inside the function so there is no external config to find, no flag to remember, no ambiguity.
// ConvoySessionManager.kt
/**
 * Returns true if the user has an active subscription.
 *
 * WALKAWAY STATE: Hardcoded to return true for all signed-in users.
 * This allows full V3.0 feature access without subscription billing.
 *
 * TO ACTIVATE SUBSCRIPTION BILLING AT GO-LIVE:
 *   1. Comment out the hardcoded 'return true' below
 *   2. Uncomment the expires_at check block
 *   3. Ensure users.expires_at is being updated by the receipt
 *      verification endpoint (convoy_api.php POST /billing/verify)
 *   4. Ensure Google Play Billing SDK is wired (see ConvoyBillingClient.kt)
 *   5. Update /users/register to stop setting expires_at = 2099-12-31
 *
 * No other code changes are required anywhere else in the app.
 * Every subscription gate calls isSubscribed() — change this, change all.
 */
fun isSubscribed(ctx: Context): Boolean {
    // WALKAWAY: return true for all signed-in users
    if (!isSignedIn(ctx)) return false
    return true
    // GO-LIVE: uncomment the block below, remove 'return true' above
    //
    // val expires = ctx.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, 0)
    //     .getLong(KEY_EXPIRES_AT, 0L)
    // return expires > System.currentTimeMillis()
}
5.3 Key API Surface on ConvoySessionManager

5.4 LaunchRoute Enum
enum class LaunchRoute {
    SIGN_IN,        // No cached user_id
    SUBSCRIPTION,   // Post go-live only; never reached at walkaway
    TERMS,          // Cached user_id, terms version mismatch
    DASHBOARD,      // All checks pass
    CONVOY_MAP      // Offline or Skip-for-now
}
6. API Endpoints — Registration Flow
File: ConvoyApiClient.kt (EXISTS)

6.1 Request/Response Contracts
POST /users/register
Request:  { google_id, email, first_name, last_name }
Response: { user_id: UUID, expires_at: datetime, is_new: bool }
At walkaway: PHP sets expires_at = 2099-12-31 for all registrations. At go-live: expires_at is set by receipt verification flow.
7. Online / Offline Behavior
KEY PRINCIPLE: Authentication state must never block radio operation. Mesh map, HUD, GPS tracking, radio config always work using locally cached data.
7.1 Pending Registration Recovery
If Google succeeds but POST /users/register fails, user is NOT forced back through Google sign-in on next attempt:
Google creds (id, email, names) cached with registration_pending=true
User routed to Convoy Map with banner: 'Sign-in pending — online features available once connected'
On every launch and connectivity change, background task retries using cached Google creds
On success, user_id cached, registration_pending cleared, s02 Terms flow triggered on next app resume
8. Paywall Stub Design Summary
8.1 Stub Mechanism
s01b paywall screen is FULLY BUILT and navigable from dev menu
isSubscribed() hardcoded to return true (see section 5.2)
resolveLaunchRoute() never routes to SUBSCRIPTION at walkaway because isSubscribed is always true
All subscription-gated screens (Dashboard, Rides, Invite, Explore, etc.) behave as if user is subscribed
users.expires_at in RDS set to 2099-12-31 for walkaway-era registrations (backup belt-and-suspenders)
Dashboard profile shows 'SUBSCRIBED' status badge
8.2 What Makes This a Safe Stub
Single point of control — only isSubscribed() changes at go-live. No scattered flags to find.
Self-documenting — activation instructions live inside the function body, not in a separate config doc.
Screen stays testable — dev menu force-route keeps s01b exercised through walkaway testing.
Reversible — hardcoded true can be re-enabled instantly if go-live encounters issues.

1. Document Purpose & Scope
This inventory catalogs all 29 atomic stubbed processes in GroupTrack V3.0, derived from comprehensive where_used analysis, real database schema inspection, and existing PHP API evaluation. Each process has explicit implementation requirements to eliminate rediscovery in future development cycles.

where_used analysis: traced function calls to identify stub patterns and integration points
Database schema inspection: documented all 66+ fields across 5 tables
PHP API gap analysis: identified 80% of database capabilities unused by current API
Android integration mapping: connected UI screens to backend requirements
1.2 Key Findings
Database capability mismatch: Sophisticated 66-field schema vs basic 20-field API usage
Advanced features already in database: map bounds, location services, terms tracking, status workflows
Implementation strategy: expand existing PHP patterns rather than rebuild from scratch
Implementation Reality: Database supports advanced features that current PHP API doesn't expose. V3.0 completion = API expansion, not database redesign.
2. Core API Backend Processes
Primary backend integration processes derived from ConvoyApiClient method signatures and real database schema requirements.

Real-time data endpoints for ConvoyDashboardScreen.kt. UI components expect these feeds but currently display placeholder data.

5. User Management & Session Processes
User account and session management. Database has 23 user fields but PHP API only uses 6 basic fields.
6. Content & Community Processes
Community content sharing and discovery features. Requires new database tables for track library and rating system.
7. GPS & Location Services
Location tracking and GPS services integration. Connects V2.4 convoy tracking with V3.0 community features.
8. Communication & Notification Systems
User communication, notifications, and messaging infrastructure for platform engagement.
9. Implementation Strategy & Priorities
Ordered implementation sequence based on user impact, technical dependencies, and platform value delivery.

SP26-SP28: Communication systems - notifications, email, real-time updates
9.3 Community Features (Network Effects)

9.4 Technical Dependencies

Step 2 — SSH to EC2 and move to web root
ssh -i ~/.ssh/convoy-api-key-2.pem ec2-user@34.224.89.217
sudo mv ~/index.html /var/www/html/index.html
Step 3 — Verify
curl -s http://localhost/ | head -5
Should return the first 5 lines of the HTML. Then test in browser: http://34.224.89.217

ssh -i ~/.ssh/convoy-api-key-2.pem ec2-user@34.224.89.217 "sudo mkdir -p /var/www/html/docs && sudo chmod 755 /var/www/html/docs"

=== GroupTrack_WhereUsed_Reference_v1.docx ===
GroupTrack
Complete Field-Level Where-Used Reference
68 Files  |  396 Functions  |  Lifecycle-Tagged Call Chains
May 2026  |  MANDATORY REFERENCE BEFORE ANY CODE CHANGE  |  Confidential
Lifecycle Phase Legend
RULE: Any function tagged INIT must NOT require permissions, network, or launch activities. Any function tagged TICK must have permission guard if it accesses GPS/Location.
1. Meshtastic Base Layer Modifications
These are changes made to files OUTSIDE the convoy/ package. Stock Meshtastic does not have these. Every change here runs during app startup and affects ALL users.
1.1 MainActivity.kt
1.2 ui/Main.kt
1.3 navigation/ConvoyNavigation.kt
1.4 app/build.gradle.kts
1.5 AndroidManifest.xml
2. ConvoyViewModel.kt — Critical Path Analysis
47 functions. This is the heart of the convoy system. Every tick cycle, every GPS call, every state update flows through here.
2.1 INIT Phase — Runs During App Startup
WARNING: Everything in init{} runs on the MAIN THREAD during Activity.onCreate(). No permissions are granted yet. No UI is visible. Any blocking call here causes ANR.
ISSUE: scanImportDirectory() runs in init via viewModelScope.launch. It queries MediaStore which may require storage permission. On a fresh install this may fail silently or block.
2.2 TICK Phase — Runs Every 3–5 Seconds
WARNING: tick() runs from init{} before map loads. Permission guard added in efa1b677e.
2.3 Tick Call Chain — Full Trace
init{} → startTick() → tick() [every 3s]
  tick() → [PERMISSION CHECK] → readLiveNodes(nowMs)
    readLiveNodes() → nodeRepository.nodeDBbyNum.value
      IF nodeMap.isEmpty() (no radio):
        → [PERMISSION CHECK] → startPhoneGps()
          → LocationManager.requestLocationUpdates(GPS_PROVIDER, 2000L, 1f, listener, mainLooper)
        → getPhoneLocation()
          → gpsService?.lastLat/lastLon (prefer ConvoyGpsService)
          → OR LocationManager.getLastKnownLocation (fallback)
        → return listOf(ConvoyNode("!phone", ...))
      IF nodeMap NOT empty (radio connected):
        → iterate nodeMap → build ConvoyNode list from radio data
  tick() → ConvoyEngine.compute(nodes, myCartId, nowMs, ...)
    compute() → computeStatus() → computeHeading() → assignLeadTail()
  tick() → _convoyState.value = state
  tick() → trail segment accumulation (if recording)
  tick() → gpsService?.onRadioPosition() (if radio has fix)
2.4 MAP-LOAD Phase
2.5 RECORD Phase
2.6 RADIO Phase
2.7 Download Functions
3. ConvoyScreen.kt — Main Convoy Map
15 exported functions. Primary UI screen. Contains WebView, HUD panels, record controls, download dialogs.
* viewModel.onMapReady() was added in commit f49cf8a3a then rolled back. Currently NOT called. Tick starts in init{} with permission guard.
4. ConvoyGpsService.kt — GPS Recording Engine
27 functions. Foreground service for GPS track recording. Independent of tick cycle.
KEY: startLocationUpdates() uses 3000ms interval. MAP-01 task: change to 1000ms for smoother tracking.
KEY: onRadioPosition() is called from tick() when radio has GPS fix. This bridges tick and GPS service.
5. ConvoyEngine.kt — Pure Computation
9 functions. Stateless convoy computation. No side effects, no I/O, no permissions. Safe to call anywhere.

Question | Answer Required
What function am I changing? | Name, file, line number
What calls this function? | Trace callers from where-used reference above
What lifecycle phase does it run in? | INIT / TICK / MAP-LOAD / RECORD / RADIO / USER
Does it run on the main thread? | YES/NO — if YES, can it block?
Does it require permissions? | List: ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, BLUETOOTH_SCAN, etc.
Are those permissions guaranteed at this phase? | INIT=NO, MAP-LOAD=MAYBE, RECORD=YES
Does it access network, GPS, or file I/O? | Any of these can block the main thread
Does it launch another Activity? | NEVER during INIT or TICK
Have I tested on a CLEAN INSTALL? | Uninstall, install, grant permissions, time startup
Have I tested on the SLOWEST device? | P10_T (3GB RAM, Android 16)

1 | Organizer | Creates ride → POST /rides → RDS stores ride with map bounds + channel + PSK
2 | Organizer | Sends invite → POST /invites → token generated, invite.json_distributed = false

4 | App | JSON receipt triggers: (a) map download queued, (b) radio_config_pending = true, (c) calendar entry stub
5 | App | On every login: GET /users/pending_invites → re-distribute any json_distributed = false invites
6 | App | Startup queue check: process pending map downloads if connected

March 23, 2026  |  Branch: feature/convoy-event-ride  |  kixazz25/Meshtastic-Android
Priority 1 — Radio Write Persistence
WorkingConfig is wiped every time the user navigates to the Meshtastic connections screen. Two separate radio reset functions are the cause. This is a field-blocking issue — the organizer cannot pair a radio mid-session without losing all config work. Must be fixed before field deployment.

Smart position broadcast interval is fixed in master config. Riders in fast-moving convoys need more frequent updates; slower rides can conserve battery with longer intervals. Slider reads live from radio, writes back only if changed — no reboot required for position config changes.

GroupTrack.org
Product Roadmap v7
Last Updated: March 22, 2026  |  Author: Fred Kix  |  Repo: kixazz25/Meshtastic-Android
Platform Overview
GroupTrack.org is a Meshtastic-based off-grid group ride coordination system built as a fork of the Meshtastic Android client. It provides real-time mesh networking for vehicle convoys, event ride organization, and field coordination without cellular dependency. Domain: GroupTrack.org.
Product Tiers and Pricing
V1 — Manual Setup Group Ride Tracker
V2 — Self-Service Setup + Backend Ride Registration
V2 Architecture

V2 Pending Features

TIER | PRICE | DESCRIPTION
Personal Edition | Free | Ships with the default master radio configuration. Supports all core tracking, HUD, recording, and map functions. All organizer, rider, and group definitions stored and managed on the GroupTrack.org online database. Full offline operation once configured.
Unique Ride Definition | $3.00/mo | Upgrade tier for groups requiring custom ride definitions. Organizer defines the ride parameters and map region. Riders pull ride configuration to automatically customize their radio settings and download map tiles for the ride area. Includes full ride definition, invite distribution, and map pre-loading. Designed for recurring group rides with unique channel and configuration requirements.

GroupTrack.org
User Manual  —  Version 2
March 2026  |  Android  |  Off-Grid Group Ride Coordination
This manual covers all screens, navigation paths, and features of GroupTrack.org V2. V2 adds self-service radio configuration, ride creation and transfer, and a fully automated binary radio config engine. No manual radio knowledge is required.

1. Installation
What You Need
Enable Installation from Unknown Sources
Android blocks apps from outside the Play Store by default. Enable this once before installing:
Android 8.0 and later:
Open Settings → Apps → Special app access → Install unknown apps
Find your email app or file manager
Toggle Allow from this source to ON
Android 7.0:
Open Settings → Security → toggle Unknown sources ON
Install the APK
Open the email containing GroupTrack-V2-debug.apk on your Android device
Tap the APK attachment to download it
Tap the downloaded file to install
Tap Install when Android prompts — if Play Protect warns, tap Install Anyway
Tap Done or Open when complete
2. First Launch and Radio Pairing
First Launch
Open GroupTrack.org from your app drawer
The map loads automatically as the home screen
The GroupTrack header and button bar appear at the bottom
Pairing Your Radio
Turn on your Meshtastic radio
On the Android device, go to Android Settings → Bluetooth and ensure Bluetooth is ON
In GroupTrack.org, tap the Meshtastic connections icon (top of screen, person/antenna icon)
Tap Scan for devices
Select your radio from the list — it will show the radio model name
Wait for CONNECTED status — the status bar turns green
3. Main Map Screen
The main map screen is the home screen of GroupTrack.org. It shows a live Leaflet map with all convoy nodes plotted as markers.
Map Layout
Main Map Screen Elements
Map Tile Modes
Map Tile Buttons
RECORD Button
The RECORD button (top-left) starts and stops GPS track recording. When recording is active, the button turns red.
RECORD Button States
4. The Button Bar
The button bar is fixed at the bottom of the screen. It controls which HUD panel is displayed over the map.
Button Bar
Button Bar → GROUP / MY CART / HIDE / GEAR
5. GROUP HUD Panel
The GROUP panel shows the overall convoy status at a glance. It is the primary view during a ride — the organizer and safety monitors should keep this panel active.
GROUP HUD Fields
6. MY CART HUD Panel
The MY CART panel shows your own vehicle's telemetry. Your cart is identified by the Bluetooth-connected radio's node ID.
MY CART HUD Fields
7. NODE HUD Panel — Individual Cart Detail
Tap any cart marker on the map to open the NODE HUD panel for that specific vehicle. The NODE panel shows full telemetry for the selected cart and provides management actions.
Map → Tap any cart marker → NODE HUD panel opens
NODE HUD Fields
NODE HUD Actions
The NODE panel includes action buttons for convoy management. Note: some actions are pending reconnection in V2 and are shown for reference.
NODE HUD Action Buttons
8. The GroupTrack Menu
Tap the GroupTrack header at the top of the screen to open the GroupTrack submenu bottom sheet. The menu contains all convoy operations organized by category.
GroupTrack header → Submenu opens
EVENT / RIDE Section
Event / Ride Menu Items
MAP SETTINGS Section
Map Settings Menu Items
9. Create a Ride
The Create a Ride screen is used by the organizer to create a new convoy ride. The app generates a unique encrypted channel name and AES-256 key automatically.
GroupTrack menu → EVENT / RIDE → Create a Ride
Email Gate
Before creating a ride, the app validates your organizer profile. If no profile exists, you are prompted to enter your email address and complete enrollment.
Create Ride Screen Fields
Create Ride Fields
Create Ride Buttons
10. Transfer Event/Ride Details via Email
The Transfer screen lets you send a ride configuration to riders via email. The ride is sent as a .convoy file attachment. When the rider taps the attachment, GroupTrack.org opens automatically and imports the ride.
GroupTrack menu → EVENT / RIDE → Transfer Event/Ride Details via Email
Transfer Screen Layout
Transfer Screen Elements
Sending a Ride
Search for your ride by organizer name, or scroll to find it
Tap the ride row to select it — checkmark appears
Tap SEND [RIDE NAME] VIA EMAIL
Select your email app from the Android share sheet
Add recipient email addresses and send
The .convoy File Format
NOTE: The .convoy file format has been superseded. Rides are now distributed via invite link through the GroupTrack.org backend API. The information below is retained for reference only.
convoyDocType — identifies the file as a convoy_ride
Ride name, date, description
Channel name and AES-256 encryption key
Organizer profile — name, email, phone, vehicle type
11. Apply Ride Info to Radio
The Apply Radio screen configures the connected Meshtastic radio for either the master baseline config or a specific ride. This is the core V2 feature — no manual radio configuration is required.
GroupTrack menu → EVENT / RIDE → Apply Ride Info to Radio
Mode Tabs
Apply Mode Tabs
Ride Selector (RIDE tab only)
In RIDE mode, a list of saved rides appears below the mode tabs. Tap a ride to select it. The selected ride's channel name appears prominently above the config detail.
Long Name Field
The Long Name field shows the radio's current name (callsign). You can edit it before applying. Leave blank to keep the existing name. The working config default is shown as placeholder text.
Channel Name Display
The new channel name is displayed prominently in large blue text above the accordion sections. In MASTER mode this shows 'Convoy'. In RIDE mode this shows the ride-specific channel (e.g. CONVOY-HD26). Verify this is correct before proceeding.
Config Accordion Groups
All config groups are collapsed by default. Tap any group header to expand and review the field values before applying. These are diagnostic — not for editing.
Config Accordion Groups
REVIEW CHANGES Screen
After selecting a mode and optionally a ride, tap REVIEW CHANGES to see the full field comparison. This shows each field with its current radio value and the new value that will be written.
Review Changes Columns
PROCEED TO UPDATE Button
The PROCEED TO UPDATE button is enabled only when the radio is connected. It is red/disabled when disconnected and green when connected. Tapping starts the two-stage radio write process.
12. ReconnectWait Screen
After tapping PROCEED TO UPDATE, the ReconnectWait screen manages the two-stage radio write process. The screen blocks navigation — only CANCEL can exit.
Stage 1 — Binary Install (38 fields)
The app installs a DeviceProfile binary to the radio. This writes 38 config fields atomically in a single transaction. The radio reboots after the write.
Stage 1 Display
Stage 2 — Channel Write (channel name + PSK)
After tapping WRITE CHANNEL + PSK, the app opens a Bluetooth edit transaction, writes the channel name, AES-256 encryption key, and position precision settings, then commits the transaction. The radio reboots to activate the new encryption key.
Stage 2 Display
Manual Bluetooth Toggle
If the radio does not reconnect automatically after either reboot, the WRITE CHANNEL or PROCEED TO VERIFY button will not enable. Follow these steps to reconnect manually:
Pull down the Android notification shade
Tap the Bluetooth tile to turn Bluetooth OFF
Wait 3 seconds
Tap the Bluetooth tile to turn Bluetooth ON
Wait for the radio to reconnect — the button will turn blue/green
13. Verify Config Screen
The Verify screen reads all 40 config fields back from the radio and compares them against the expected values. Only failed fields are displayed. Passed fields show as group summaries.
Verify Screen Layout
Verify Screen Elements
40 Verified Fields
Field Groups
14. Restore Prior Config Post Ride
Before every radio config apply, GroupTrack.org automatically saves a full backup of the current radio state as a .cfg binary file. The Archive Restore screen lets you select and restore any saved backup.
GroupTrack menu → EVENT / RIDE → Restore Prior Config Post Ride
Archive List
Archives are listed newest first for the currently connected radio node. Each archive shows the date and time it was captured, the filename, and the file size.
Archive List Columns
Restore Process
Connect your radio via Bluetooth
Tap GroupTrack menu → Restore Prior Config Post Ride
Tap the archive you want to restore
Review the warning: RESTORE WILL OVERWRITE CURRENT RADIO CONFIG
Tap RESTORE THIS ARCHIVE (orange button — only enabled when radio is connected)
Wait 60 seconds for the radio to reboot
Radio is restored to the selected backup state
15. Developer Settings Panel
The Settings Panel is a password-protected developer screen for managing the master config and apply list. Access requires the convoy admin password.
Long press GroupTrack header → Enter password → Settings Panel opens
Settings Panel Options
Settings Panel Items
Apply List Checklist
The apply list controls which fields are overwritten when applying master config. Each field has a checkbox:
CHECKED — field value comes from master_config.json (convoy standard)
UNCHECKED — field value is preserved from the radio's current config (e.g. hardware-specific GPIO settings)
Capture Master Config
Use Capture Master Config when the reference radio has been updated with new settings (e.g. new firmware, new region, new telemetry intervals). The capture reads all fields from the connected radio and saves three files:
master.cfg — binary DeviceProfile for atomic import
master_config.json — human-readable JSON for the rules engine
convoy_apply_list.json — field apply rules
16. Rider Workflow — Complete End-to-End
This section covers the complete workflow for a rider receiving a ride invitation and configuring their radio.
Step 1 — Install the App
If not already installed: follow Section 1. Installation. The app only needs to be installed once.
Step 2 — Receive the Ride Email
Organizer sends a .convoy file to your email address
Open the email on your Android device
Tap the .convoy attachment
Android opens GroupTrack.org automatically (no app chooser)
The file is saved to the import queue
Step 3 — Confirm Import
Open GroupTrack.org
Tap the GroupTrack header to open the menu
If a ride was imported, a splash screen appears for 3 seconds: NEW RIDE IMPORTED: [ride name]
The splash screen dismisses automatically — the menu opens normally
Step 4 — Configure Your Radio
Connect your Meshtastic radio via Bluetooth
Tap GroupTrack menu → Apply Ride Info to Radio
Select the RIDE tab
Tap the imported ride in the list
Verify the channel name displayed is correct for your ride
Tap REVIEW CHANGES
Optionally edit your Long Name (callsign)
Tap PROCEED TO UPDATE
Stage 1: Wait for 60-second countdown. WRITE CHANNEL + PSK button turns blue.
Tap WRITE CHANNEL + PSK
Stage 2: Wait for 60-second countdown. PROCEED TO VERIFY button turns green.
Tap PROCEED TO VERIFY
Verify screen shows all 40 fields ✓ — radio is configured for the ride
Step 5 — Confirm on Ride Day
Turn on radio before leaving home — allow 2 minutes for GPS lock
Open GroupTrack.org — your cart appears on the map
Verify GROUP HUD shows other convoy members as they join
Confirm ACTIVE count matches expected number of vehicles

18. Troubleshooting
Feedback and Bug Reports
Report issues directly to the project lead. Include:
Android device model and Android version (Settings → About phone)
Meshtastic radio model and firmware version
Description of what happened and what you expected
Screenshot or logcat output if possible
GroupTrack.org  |  User Manual V2  |  March 23, 2026  |  Built on Meshtastic open-source platform
ℹ INFO: GroupTrack.org requires a paired Meshtastic-compatible LoRa radio. All convoy coordination happens over the radio mesh — no cellular or internet connection required during rides.
Android Device | Android 8.0 (Oreo) or later. Tablet recommended for map visibility.
Meshtastic Radio | SenseCAP T1000-E (recommended), T-Beam v2, or any Meshtastic LoRa device running firmware 2.6+
Bluetooth | Required to pair Android device with radio
Storage | Approximately 100 MB free
APK File | GroupTrack-V2-debug.apk — sent via email attachment
✓ TIP: You only need to enable Unknown Sources once. You can disable it again after installation.
ℹ INFO: Keep the radio powered and within 10 metres of your phone during config. Once configured, range extends to the mesh network distance (typically 1-5km line of sight).
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Map Area | Full-screen Leaflet map showing node positions. Pinch to zoom, drag to pan.
GroupTrack header | Tappable header at top. Opens the GroupTrack submenu.
RECORD button | Top-left corner. Red dot icon. Tap to start/stop GPS track recording.
Map tile buttons | Top-right corner. SAT | HYB | RD — switch between satellite, hybrid, and road map tiles.
Node markers | Each convoy vehicle shown as a labeled circle. Your cart is larger. Tap to open NODE HUD.

SAT (Satellite) | Satellite imagery. Best for terrain awareness in remote areas.
HYB (Hybrid) | Satellite + road overlay. Best balance of terrain and navigation.
⚠ NOTE: Map tiles require an internet connection. Download cached tiles before heading into areas with no cell service. Cached tiles are stored on-device and available offline.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Grey circle | Recording OFF — tap to start recording
Red circle | Recording ACTIVE — tap to stop and save
✓ TIP: The file save dialog appears when you tap STOP (END RECORD), not when you start. Name your track at the end so you can give it a meaningful name based on the actual ride.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
GROUP | Shows the GROUP HUD panel — convoy-wide status: all carts, span, lead, tail.
MY CART | Shows the MY CART HUD panel — your vehicle's individual stats.
HIDE | Hides the HUD overlay completely — map-only view for maximum visibility.
GEAR (⚙) | Opens map settings and layer controls. Tile source, filter options.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Ride Title | Name of the active ride (e.g. HIGH DESERT RUN 2026).
UNITS | Total number of cart nodes known to the mesh network.
ACTIVE | Vehicles heard recently — within the last broadcast interval.
LOST | Vehicles that have gone silent — not heard for the lost threshold period.
LEAD | Callsign of the frontmost vehicle (green). Determined automatically by position.
TAIL | Callsign of the rearmost vehicle (orange). Determined automatically by position.
SPAN | Distance in miles from the LEAD vehicle to the TAIL vehicle.
ℹ INFO: LEAD and TAIL are determined automatically each update cycle based on GPS positions relative to the direction of travel. No manual assignment is required.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Callsign | Your vehicle's convoy callsign (e.g. INDIA-7). Derived from radio node name.
SPD | Current speed in mph (Imperial setting) or km/h (Metric).
HDG | Heading in degrees (0-359). 0 = North, 90 = East, 180 = South, 270 = West.
BAT | Radio battery percentage. Updates with each telemetry packet.
ALT | Altitude in feet (Imperial) or meters (Metric).
AHEAD | Distance to the nearest vehicle ahead of you in the convoy order.
BEHIND | Distance to the nearest vehicle behind you in the convoy order.
TO LEAD | Distance to the LEAD vehicle.
TO TAIL | Distance to the TAIL vehicle.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Cart Name | Convoy callsign of the selected cart (e.g. GOLF-8).
Status | ACTIVE, SIGNAL DROP, or LOST — based on last heard time.
SPD | Current speed of the selected cart.
HDG | Heading of the selected cart.
BAT | Battery percentage of the selected cart's radio.
SNR | Signal-to-noise ratio of the last received packet — indicates radio link quality.
ALT | Altitude of the selected cart.
Position in convoy | Order position: e.g. 3 of 8 — third cart from the front.
Last seen | Time since the last position packet was received from this cart.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
RETURN | Returns map view to the full convoy — exits node focus mode.
SET AS LEAD | Designates this cart as the LEAD vehicle. Shows confirmation dialog if no lead is set. (Pending V2 reconnection)
REMOVE FROM RIDE | Removes this cart from the active ride roster. Used when a vehicle drops out mid-ride. (Pending V2 reconnection)
✓ TIP: Tap the cart marker again or tap RETURN to dismiss the NODE HUD and return to GROUP or MY CART view.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Create a Ride | Opens the ride creation screen. Organizer creates a new ride with name, date, channel, and encryption key.
Transfer Event/Ride Details via Email | Opens the ride transfer screen. Select a ride and send it to riders as a .convoy email attachment.
Apply Ride Info to Radio | Opens the radio config screen. Apply MASTER config or a specific ride config to the connected radio.
Restore Prior Config Post Ride | Opens the archive restore screen. Select and restore a saved radio backup.

Offline Maps & Tile Management | Coming in V3 — manage offline tile regions for areas without cell service.
✓ TIP: The GEAR button on the button bar also opens map layer controls for quick tile switching without opening the full menu.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Ride Name | Name for the ride (e.g. HIGH DESERT RUN 2026). This becomes the channel name prefix.
Ride Date | Scheduled date for the ride. Used for sorting in the ride list.
Description | Optional text description of the ride — route notes, meeting point, etc.
Channel Name | Auto-generated from ride name: CONVOY-XXXX format (max 11 characters). Can be edited.
Encryption Key | Auto-generated AES-256 key. Shown as ****. Tap to view. Unique per ride.
Organizer Info | Pre-filled from your enrollment profile: name, email, phone, vehicle type.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
SAVE RIDE | Saves the ride to the local database. Ride appears in Apply Radio RIDE tab and Transfer screen.
CANCEL | Discards the new ride and returns to the map.
⚠ NOTE: The channel name and encryption key are generated once and cannot be regenerated. Copy or screenshot them before leaving the screen if needed for manual radio config.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Search bar | Filter rides by organizer name. Type any part of first or last name.
Ride list | All saved rides displayed as rows. Future rides shown with green dot. Past rides shown dimmed.
Ride row columns | NAME — DATE — ORGANIZER — CHANNEL. Tap a row to select it.
Selection indicator | Checkmark (✓) appears on selected ride. Tap again to deselect.
SEND button | Appears blue when a ride is selected. Shows ride name. Tap to open share sheet.
CANCEL | Returns to map without sending.
ℹ INFO: The .convoy format is extensible. Future versions will support convoy_map_region (offline map tile URLs), convoy_route (KML routes), and convoy_master (master radio config transfer).
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
MASTER tab | Applies the master baseline config. Resets the radio to the standard convoy baseline: US region, LONG_FAST preset, 60s GPS, Convoy channel, AES-256 master key.
RIDE tab | Applies a specific ride config. Uses master baseline plus the ride's unique channel name and AES-256 encryption key. Only radios with the same ride config can communicate.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
LORA | LoRa radio settings: region, modem preset, bandwidth, spread factor, coding rate, hop limit, TX enabled, TX power.
CHANNEL | Channel name, encryption key status, uplink/downlink enabled, position precision, mute status.
DEVICE | Node role, managed mode, serial enabled.
POSITION | GPS broadcast interval, GPS update interval, smart position settings, fixed position, position flags.
DISPLAY | Display units (Imperial/Metric), screen timeout, auto brightness, compass orientation.
MODULE | Telemetry intervals, MQTT settings, serial module, notifications, range test, store/forward, neighbor info, detection sensor, audio.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
FIELD | The radio config field name.
CURRENT | The current value on the radio.
NEW VALUE | The value that will be written to the radio.
SOURCE | Where the new value comes from: CHECKLIST (master config), ORIGINAL RADIO (kept from radio), or RIDE FILE (ride-specific override).
⚠ NOTE: The apply process writes 40 fields to the radio in two stages across two reboots. Total time is approximately 2-3 minutes. Do not disconnect the radio during this process.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Stage indicator | STAGE 1 OF 2 shown at top.
Countdown timer | 60-second countdown. Radio needs this time to complete the reboot.
Status message | Shows current phase: Binary install reboot — please wait... Xs
WRITE CHANNEL + PSK button | Appears blue after 60s when radio has reconnected. Disabled (grey) during countdown.
⚠ NOTE: Do not tap WRITE CHANNEL + PSK until the button turns blue. The button only enables after the full 60 seconds AND the radio has reconnected via Bluetooth.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Stage indicator | STAGE 2 OF 2 shown at top.
Countdown timer | 60-second countdown for channel write reboot.
PROCEED TO VERIFY button | Appears green after 60s when radio has reconnected. Tap to proceed to verification.
ℹ INFO: This manual toggle is necessary because Android 13+ blocks automated Bluetooth toggling from apps. This is an Android OS limitation, not an app bug.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Connection status | Green: RADIO CONNECTED. Red: RADIO NOT CONNECTED — waiting.
Overall result banner | ALL X FIELDS VERIFIED (green) or X of X fields failed (red).
Failed fields table | FIELD — EXPECTED — ACTUAL — GROUP. Only shown if there are failures.
Group summary | Shows pass/fail count per group: Device, LoRa, Channel, Position, Display, Module.
DONE button | Green if all passed. Orange with failure count if any failed. Always tappable to exit.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Device (4 fields) | Long Name (write-only), Node Role, Managed Mode, Serial Enabled.
LoRa (8 fields) | Region, Modem Preset, Bandwidth, Spread Factor, Coding Rate, Hop Limit, TX Enabled, TX Power.
Channel (4 fields) | Channel Name, Encryption Key (32-byte check), Position Precision, Channel Is Muted.
Position (6 fields) | Broadcast Interval, GPS Update Interval, Smart Position, Smart Min Interval, Smart Min Distance, Fixed Position.
Display (4 fields) | Display Units, Screen Timeout, Auto Brightness (informational), Compass North Top.
Module (14 fields) | Telemetry x3, MQTT x5, Serial, Ext Notification, Range Test, Store Forward, Neighbor Info, Detection Sensor, Audio. (Set by binary install — marked as informational until moduleConfigFlow is wired.)
! IMPORTANT: If the Verify screen shows Channel Name or Encryption Key failures, the channel write did not complete correctly. Run Apply Radio again and ensure both Stage 1 and Stage 2 complete fully before proceeding to Verify.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
Date/Time | When the backup was captured. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS
Filename | Full archive filename including node ID, timestamp, and label (e.g. pre_master).
Size | File size in bytes.
Selection | Tap a row to select it. Checkmark appears. Tap again to deselect.
⚠ NOTE: Archive restore only writes the binary config fields (38 fields). It does not restore the channel name and PSK. After restoring, run Apply Master to re-apply the channel and encryption key if needed.
ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
EDIT APPLY LIST | Opens the apply list checklist. Each field can be checked (use master value) or unchecked (keep radio value). Changes saved immediately.
RESTORE FROM ARCHIVE | Opens the Archive Restore screen. Same as the convoy menu item.
CAPTURE MASTER CONFIG | Reads all 40 fields from the connected radio and saves them as master_config.json and master.cfg. These become the new baseline for all future applies.
! IMPORTANT: The apply list is an advanced feature. Do not uncheck fields unless you understand the impact. Incorrect settings can prevent the radio from operating on the convoy mesh.
⚠ NOTE: After capturing new master assets, the developer must pull the files via ADB, commit them to the repository, and rebuild and redistribute the APK for the new baseline to take effect for all users.
✓ TIP: Your radio is now configured with the ride's encrypted channel. Only riders with the same ride config can communicate on this channel.
FIELD | VALUE | NOTES
Region | US (915 MHz) | Required for legal operation in USA
Modem Preset | LONG_FAST | Best range/speed balance for convoy use
Hop Limit | 3 | Max 3 mesh hops — sufficient for convoy spread
TX Power | 27 dBm | Maximum legal power for US 915 MHz
GPS Broadcast | 60 seconds | Position shared every 60s or on 100m movement
Smart Position | Enabled | Sends position on 100m movement regardless of timer
Smart Min Distance | 100 meters | Minimum movement before smart position fires
GPS Update Interval | 1 second | GPS chip polls every 1 second
Display Units | Imperial | Miles, feet, mph
Screen Timeout | 300 seconds | Screen stays on 5 minutes
Node Role | TRACKER | Optimized for GPS tracking — reduces non-tracking transmissions
Channel Name | Convoy | Master baseline channel. Rides get CONVOY-XXXX.
Position Precision | 32 (full) | Exact GPS position shared — required for convoy tracking
Encryption | AES-256 | Unique 32-byte key per ride
STATUS | MEANING
ACTIVE | Vehicle heard recently — operating normally
SIGNAL DROP | Vehicle not heard for signal drop threshold — may be temporarily out of range
LOST | Vehicle not heard for lost threshold — treat as potentially missing
OFF TRACK | Vehicle more than 150 feet from route trail — callsign label turns red on map
PROBLEM | SOLUTION
No vehicles on map | Check radio is connected (green in Meshtastic). Verify all radios use same channel name and PSK.
Yellow lock icon on radio | Encryption not active. Run Apply Radio again — complete both Stage 1 and Stage 2 fully.
WRITE CHANNEL button does not turn blue | Radio has not reconnected. Toggle Bluetooth OFF then ON manually. Wait 10 seconds.
Verify screen shows channel failures | Channel write did not complete. Run Apply Radio again. Allow full 60s for each stage.
Imported ride not appearing | Open GroupTrack menu — if splash appears, import is processing. If not, resend the ride from the organizer.
RECORD button not tappable | Cart status messages may overlay the button. Dismiss status messages or relaunch the app.
Map not showing correct zoom | Initial zoom set on screen entry. Use pinch to zoom. If map snaps back, this is a known issue (UI-09) pending fix.
NODE HUD not opening on cart tap | Cart tap detail panel pending reconnection in V2 (UI-06). Known issue.
Play Protect warning on install | Tap Install Anyway. Expected for APKs distributed outside the Play Store.
Radio shows CLIENT role after apply | Verify master_config.json has nodeRole: TRACKER. Recapture master if needed.
Stage 1 countdown completes but no reconnect | Radio may not have rebooted. Check radio power light. If off, power cycle. Then toggle BT.
App closes when navigating to BT settings | Known persistence issue (UI-NEW-04) — pending fix. Restart Apply Radio from menu.
